what: The command post's plan wording (wordPlan with the wording's own on-device options and JSON constraint, the same as CommandPost's suggest uses on the built-in model), measured on a local page with the same code path (local page, same code path). One made-up plan (two teams, CC and CD, four ranked segments) worded three times in a row in a newly opened page, twice.
browser: Stephen's Google Chrome stable on this Mac (macOS, Apple M5 Pro); the built-in model reported available for text; the Chrome and model versions were not recorded
page: web/harness/wording-measure.html (dev server http://127.0.0.1:5175), bare Firebase app with no App Check and no sign-in. Sessions 1 and 2 ran a draft of the page that built the command post's own PREFER_ON_DEVICE model (wordingGenerator); every reply ran on device, so no cloud call was made. The committed page builds the same on-device options ONLY_ON_DEVICE (wordingOnDeviceGenerator), because a dev page never builds a cloud model.
note: Session 1 recorded only the kind of failure; session 2's page also kept each raw reply and the check's reason. The command post gives a wording reply 15,000 ms (REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS).

reasons: T1 searches CC due to its highest percentage change.
T2 searches CD due to its highest percentage change.
runs.summary: Teams T1 and T2 are assigned to search CC and CD, respectively, based on their recently increased percentages.
T1 is assigned to CC because of its high priority, and T2 is assigned to CD for the same reason.

runs.reason: team ids differ from the draft
runs.detail: the reply repeated T1 and T2 six times each, 12 assignments, the schema's maxItems

findings: All six wordings ran on device as the SDK reported, from 3,050 to 12,340 ms, and the pages made no request to a Google or Firebase host.
Code accepted 2 of 6; the plan then showed the fixed wording for the other 4. The one rejection with a recorded reason was a reply that repeated the teams up to the schema's 12-item limit.
Both accepted wordings kept to the plan's segments and numbers; their reasons are generic ("high-priority segment").
